facts.evidence: Net revenues rose to **$21.3 billion** (vs. **$16.8 billion** in Q2 2025), marking a record quarterly figure.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was **$5.6 billion**, or **$3.46 per diluted share** (vs. **$3.5 billion**, or **$2.13 per diluted share** in Q2 2025).
**Institutional Securities** generated **$11.0 billion** in net revenues (vs. **$7.6 billion** in Q2 2025)
**Return on tangible common equity (ROTCE)** was **26.6%** (vs. **18.2%** in Q2 2025).
**Equity revenues of $6.3 billion** (up **69%** YoY), reflecting strong client engagement and market conditions.
**Wealth Management** reported **$8.9 billion** in net revenues (vs. **$7.8 billion** in Q2 2025) ... A **pre-tax margin of 30.5%**
**$148 billion in net new assets**, including **$39.1 billion in fee-based asset flows**. ... While net new assets were a record **$148 billion**
The Board reauthorized a **$20 billion share repurchase program** beginning in Q3 2026.
The **Standardized Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio** was **14.8%** (vs. **15.0%** in Q2 2025).

claims.claim: Net revenues rose to $21.3 billion in Q2 2026, compared with $16.8 billion in Q2 2025.
The Q2 2026 net revenue figure was a record quarterly figure.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion, or $3.46 per diluted share, in Q2 2026.
Q2 2025 net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $3.5 billion, or $2.13 per diluted share.
Pre-tax income reached $7.3 billion in Q2 2026, up from $4.6 billion in Q2 2025.
The expense efficiency ratio improved to 65% in Q2 2026 from 71% in Q2 2025.
Return on tangible common equity was 26.6% in Q2 2026 versus 18.2% in Q2 2025.
Institutional Securities generated $11.0 billion in net revenues in Q2 2026 versus $7.6 billion in Q2 2025.
Institutional Securities Equity revenues were $6.3 billion, up 69% year over year.
Equity results reflected strong client engagement and favorable market conditions.
Investment Banking revenues were $2.4 billion, up 58% year over year.
Investment Banking gains came from advisory, equity underwriting and fixed income underwriting, each of which increased.
Wealth Management reported $8.9 billion in net revenues in Q2 2026 versus $7.8 billion in Q2 2025.
Wealth Management added $148 billion in net new assets in the quarter, a record.
The $148 billion of net new assets included $39.1 billion in fee-based asset flows.
claims.note: The release presents fee-based asset flows ($39.1B) and net new assets ($148.1B) as two separate metrics ("added net new assets of $148 billion and fee-based assets of $39 billion"); it never states fee-based flows are a component of NNA. The release's disclosed composition is that just over half of the $148B was inflows related to IPOs of certain Workplace-channel clients.

claims.claim: Wealth Management's pre-tax margin was 30.5%.
The Wealth Management pre-tax margin was supported by asset management fees, transactional revenues, and net interest income.
claims.note: Reported transactional revenues fell year over year ($1,167M vs $1,264M); the release says they increased only excluding prior-year DCP mark-to-market gains. The release attributes record net revenues (not the margin) to asset management fees, robust client activity and higher net interest income.

claims.claim: Investment Management recorded $1.6 billion in net revenues in Q2 2026 versus $1.55 billion in Q2 2025.
Investment Management had $7.5 billion in long-term net flows in the quarter.
No forward-looking guidance was provided in the release.
The Board reauthorized a $20 billion share repurchase program beginning in Q3 2026.
The Standardized CET1 capital ratio was 14.8%, versus 15.0% in Q2 2025.
Book value per share increased to $67.80 from $61.59 in Q2 2025.
Tangible book value per share rose to $53.18 from $47.25 in Q2 2025.
The firm repurchased $1.5 billion of common stock in Q2 2026.
The provision for credit losses was $98 million in Q2 2026 versus $196 million in Q2 2025.
The release notes growth in corporate loans and individual assessments for commercial real estate loans.
Investment Management long-term net flows of $7.5 billion were down from $12.2 billion in Q2 2025.
Compensation expense rose $997 million year over year, to $8.2 billion.
claims.note: The $8.2 billion level is in the release ($8,187M), but the $997 million year-over-year dollar increase is not disclosed; it requires subtracting $7,190M, a calculation the release does not show (it shows only a 14% change).

claims.claim: Non-compensation expenses increased $931 million, to $5.7 billion.
claims.note: The $5.7 billion level is in the release ($5,715M), but the $931 million dollar increase is not disclosed; it requires subtracting $4,784M, a calculation the release does not show (it shows only a 19% change).
